t: Patients Rescued from Unlicensed Rehabilitation Centre in South Africa
e: Authorities in South Africa have rescued around 200 patients who were found held in horrific conditions at a suspected illegal rehabilitation facility.

t: Armed Parent and Teacher Intervene in Oregon School Attack, BBC Reports
e: A teacher and an armed parent intervened to stop a 16-year-old former student who targeted an Oregon primary school classroom, according to BBC News.

t: Trump Waives Several Russia Sanctions Citing National Security
e: US President Donald Trump has temporarily lifted several Congress-passed sanctions against Moscow amid a growing dispute with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, according to BBC News.

t: Brazil Records Fall in Amazon Deforestation Ahead of Key Election
e: A report by BBC News highlights a record fall in Amazon deforestation in Brazil as the country prepares for a crucial election.

t: Ukraine Advances in Donbas Offensive as Starlink Proves Crucial, BBC Reports
e: Ukrainian forces regain key territory in the Donbas under Operation Vivaldi, though political uncertainties shadow military gains, according to BBC News.

t: Ministry Clears Arua Doctor After Minister Kawooya Orders Suspension Over Hands in Pockets
e: The Ministry of Health has clarified that senior dental surgeon Dr Robert Candia of Arua Regional Referral Hospital was never suspended, despite State Minister for Health Anifa Kawooya ordering his immediate removal during a hospital inspection after he spoke to her with his hands in his pockets. The incident triggered widespread public and professional backlash.

t: Ship Attacks Near Strait of Hormuz Reach Record High, BBC Reports
e: Reports of ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz have reached a record high as oil exports slow, according to an analysis by BBC News.

t: Fashion Designer Anita Beryl Marries Richard Ekoot in Italy
e: Ugandan fashion designer and founder of BerylQouture, Anita Beryl, has married Richard Ekoot in a wedding ceremony held in Como, Italy.

t: Riazat Ali Shah Leads Uganda Cricket Cranes for T20 World Cup Qualifiers
e: Captain Riazat Ali Shah will lead a 14-man Uganda Cricket Cranes squad in the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup Africa Sub-Regional Qualifier C in Abuja, Nigeria, from 18 to 25 October.

t: Crested Cranes’ Olympic Dream Ends After 4-1 Defeat to Zambia
e: Uganda’s Crested Cranes have been eliminated from the 2028 Olympic Games qualifiers after suffering a 4-1 defeat to Zambia in Ndola, losing 5-3 on aggregate.

t: Nineteen Injured as Bus Collides with Stopped Train Near Channel Tunnel
e: Nineteen people were injured after a bus struck a stationary train on the French side of the Channel Tunnel, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Bank of Uganda Raises Central Bank Rate to 12% to Defend Shilling
e: The Bank of Uganda has raised its Central Bank Rate by 2.25 percentage points to 12% in a special Monetary Policy Committee meeting, citing a weaker shilling, higher oil prices and rising inflation risks.

t: Uganda and South Sudan Sign Trade MoU to Ease Border Delays and Boost Commerce
e: Uganda and South Sudan have signed a memorandum of understanding on trade aimed at reducing border delays, cutting costs for traders and expanding commercial opportunities between the two countries.

t: Uganda and Kenya Agree to Scrap Remaining Barriers Choking Cross-Border Trade
e: Uganda and Kenya have agreed to eliminate remaining non-tariff barriers restricting the free movement of goods, reaffirming their commitment to the East African Community Common Market.

t: Fertilizer Costs Rise as Iran Crisis Disrupts Global Supplies
e: Ugandan farmers are facing higher fertilizer prices as disruptions to international supplies linked to the Iran crisis raise concerns about the cost of agricultural production for the coming planting seasons.

t: Maduro Denies New Torture-Related Charges in New York Court
e: Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro has pleaded not guilty to newly added torture charges in a New York court, according to BBC News.

t: 75,000-Year-Old Neanderthal Spear Wound Hints at Early Violence, Reports BBC
e: A 75,000-year-old Neanderthal spear wound suggests that lethal interpersonal violence shaped early human history earlier than previously thought, according to a BBC News report.

t: At Least 34 Dead After School Roof Collapses in Pakistan
e: At least 33 pupils and a teacher have died after a school roof collapsed in Pakistan, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Emergency Teams Respond to Peshawar School Roof Collapse
e: Rescue services in Peshawar, Pakistan, are responding to a school roof collapse after students reported hearing a cracking sound.

t: Starlink Restrictions Impacting Ukrainian Front Line Operations, Officials Say
e: Recent restrictions on Elon Musk's Starlink satellite system are affecting Ukraine's front-line drone and defense operations, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Former DR Congo President Kabila Named Leader of New Rebel Coalition
e: Former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila has been named leader of a new rebel coalition linked to M23, according to BBC News.

t: Emergency Records Reveal Confusion After Failed Execution of Christa Pike
e: Newly released emergency call records detail confusion following the botched execution attempt of death row inmate Christa Pike, who survived two lethal injection doses.

t: CCTV Footage Shows People Taking Cover During Riyadh Airport Missile Strike
e: Newly released CCTV footage shows individuals taking cover inside Riyadh airport following a missile strike on Saturday, according to BBC News.

t: US Immigration Agents Search Home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, BBC Reports
e: Federal immigration agents have searched the home of US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, according to a report by BBC News.

t: French Middle School Student Arrested After Shooting Injures Two Educators
e: A 14-year-old pupil has been detained in France after a middle-school principal and a teacher were injured in a shooting.

t: Zelensky Welcomes Proposed 'Energy Ceasefire' as Moscow Remains Silent
e: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced support for a proposed energy infrastructure truce, while Russia has yet to comment.

t: Dozens Killed in Strikes on Egypt-Sudan Border Gold Mine, Rights Group Reports
e: Dozens of gold prospectors were allegedly killed in airstrikes at a border mining camp, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Trump Claims Energy Ceasefire Deal, According to BBC Report
e: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a proposed energy ceasefire in a social media post, catching Ukraine by surprise while Russia has yet to comment.

t: Report: Falsified Documents Used to Evade Taxes on Abramovich Wealth
e: An investigation by BBC News reveals that backdated documents were used to hide yachts and mansions belonging to Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich.

t: Powderfinger Announces First Tour in 17 Years Following Reunion
e: Iconic Australian band Powderfinger has announced its first tour in 17 years after revealing their reunion, according to a report by BBC News.

t: Rescued Orangutans Returned to Borneo Forests Following Wildfires
e: Wildlife teams in Borneo have reintroduced orangutans into the wild after intense summer blazes threatened their natural habitats, according to BBC News.

t: Polish Authorities Detain Man Suspected of Plotting Attack on PM Donald Tusk
e: Polish law enforcement has detained a man suspected of planning an attack against Prime Minister Donald Tusk and his defence minister, following reports by BBC News.

t: Flash Floods Cause Widespread Damage in Central Nepal
e: Severe flash flooding along Nepal's Budhi Gandaki River has swept away buildings and bridges, according to reports by BBC News.

t: Polish PM Donald Tusk Attributes Recent School Stabbings to Online Violence
e: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has warned that the glorification of violence online is driving recent school attacks in the country, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: At Least 139 Dead After Boat Capsizes Off Djibouti Coast, UN Reports
e: At least 139 people, including children, have died after a vessel carrying 305 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Pope Leo to Undergo Surgery Following Lung Nodule Discovery
e: Pope Leo is set to undergo surgery after a lump was found on his lung at an early stage, according to reports by BBC News.

t: Report: Young Men in Myanmar Face Forced Recruitment Amid Rising Conflict
e: Young men in Myanmar live in fear of being forcibly abducted into military service, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: US Justice Department Probes TV Networks Over Trump Media Pool Coverage
e: The US Department of Justice is investigating television networks following press pool restrictions triggered by White House access blocks, according to BBC News.

t: At Least 15 Dead in Russian Glide Bomb Strike on Zaporizhzhia
e: At least 15 people, including children, have been killed in a Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Trial Underway for Murdered Australian Surfers and American Friend in Mexico
e: A court trial has unfolded in Mexico regarding the murder of two Australian surfers and their American friend two years ago.

t: New Body Camera Footage Released Following New York City ICE Shooting
e: Newly released police body camera footage captures the tense moments following a shooting involving ICE officers in New York City, according to BBC News.

t: Hundreds Detained in Delhi Following Protest Over Electoral Reforms
e: Leaders of an unregistered political group have been detained in Delhi during a demonstration calling for electoral reforms ahead of key state elections.

t: Three Injured in Third Polish School Knife Attack Within a Week
e: Polish authorities are responding to a third knife attack at a school in a single week after a woman injured three people.

t: Expedition Launched to Search for Amelia Earhart's Missing Plane
e: A new expedition is en route to a remote island in an effort to solve the 1937 disappearance of aviator Amelia Earhart, according to BBC News.

t: US Pentagon Plans Livestream of Fort Hood Shooter Execution, BBC Reports
e: The US Pentagon plans to livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan, according to a report by BBC News.

t: UAE Says Flydubai Co-Pilot Began Radicalisation in Australia, According to BBC
e: Reporting by BBC News highlights allegations by the UAE attorney-general that a Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash an aircraft into Tel Aviv's airport.

t: Trump's Russia Deal Signals Pressure Over Fuel Prices, Reports BBC
e: A recent analysis highlights efforts by the US president to curb fuel prices ahead of next month's midterm elections.

t: Tornado Sweeps Through Sicilian Town and City, Causing Damage
e: A tornado has caused damage to buildings and vehicles in Marsala and Petrosino, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Three Found Guilty in Murder of Australian Surfers and American Friend, BBC Reports
e: Three men have been convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and US friend Carter Rhoad, according to BBC News.

t: Peruvian District Elects Mayor Named Hitler Mussolini, BBC Reports
e: A left-wing candidate named Hitler Mussolini has secured a narrow mayoral victory in Peru, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Two Stolen Renoir Artworks Recovered in France
e: Two paintings by Pierre-Auguste Renoir stolen from a French Riviera museum last month have been recovered.

t: Three Killed in Houthi Missile Attack on Riyadh Airport, BBC Reports
e: Three Saudi nationals have been killed in a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport amid heightened conflict, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Navi Pillay Awarded Nobel Peace Prize for International Law Efforts
e: Former UN human rights chief Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Rwandan Genocide Suspect Dr Vincent Brown to Stand Trial in UK
e: A doctor accused of participating as a leader during the 1994 Rwandan genocide is set to face trial in the United Kingdom, according to BBC News.

t: Thieves Steal 30,000 Wine Bottles Worth €5m in Italy
e: A Florence-based winery has suffered one of the largest wine thefts in Italian history after thieves made off with €5m worth of stock.

t: France Pledges 3,000 Additional Teachers Following Student Protests
e: The French government has offered to recruit 3,000 extra teachers in an effort to calm nationwide high-school student demonstrations.

t: Kyiv Residents Prepare to Flee as Energy Infrastructure Strikes Threaten Winter Power
e: A renewed wave of Russian strikes on energy infrastructure has left many Kyiv residents contemplating leaving the capital as winter sets in, according to BBC News.

t: South Africa Experiences Fresh Outbreak of Anti-Migrant Violence
e: Cars have been torched and shops looted in South Africa during a new wave of anti-migrant violence, according to a report by BBC News.

t: ICE Agent Shoots Man in New York City
e: An ICE agent shot a man in New York City during an arrest operation, drawing outrage from the city's mayor, according to BBC News.

t: Canadian Poet Anne Carson Awarded Nobel Literature Prize
e: Canadian poet Anne Carson, 76, has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for her work crossing poetry, fiction, and scholarship, BBC News reports.

t: Monaco Bombing Suspect Speaks Out Over Attempted Assassination of Ukrainian Millionaire
e: Vitalii Zhykovych has given his account to BBC News regarding the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev in Monaco.

t: Indonesian Teacher Convicted of Pupil Abuse Returned to Prison Following Investigation
e: Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani has been returned to jail in Indonesia after secretly serving less than half his sentence.

t: Spanish Pensioner Whose Eviction Sparked Protests Passes Away, BBC Reports
e: Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old Spanish pensioner whose eviction from her long-time home sparked nationwide protests, has died.

t: Apollo 11 Software Director Margaret Hamilton Dies at 90
e: Pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton, who led the development of NASA's Apollo mission software, has passed away at age 90.

t: Texas Carries Out First US Execution Following Botched Injection Case, Reports BBC
e: Texas has executed inmate Jamaal Howard in the first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injections, according to reporting by BBC News.

t: Edward Rukidi Nyabongo I Crowned New Omukama of Tooro as Museveni Presides
e: Former UBC journalist Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma has been installed as the new Omukama of Tooro, taking the regnal name Edward Rukidi Nyabongo I, in traditional rituals at Karuziika Palace. President Museveni presided over the coronation ceremony.

t: Bishop Tells New Tooro King: One Wife, One Woman
e: The Bishop of Ruwenzori Diocese, Rt Rev Reuben Kisembo, has urged the newly crowned Omukama of Tooro, Edward Rukidi Nyabongo I, to remain faithful to his wife and uphold Christian monogamy while also calling for accountability in the management of kingdom resources.

t: Three Die in Nansana House Fire as Landlady Suspected of Arson
e: Three people, including the landlady, died in a house fire in Nansana early Monday in what police are treating as suspected arson. The landlady is believed to have set the building ablaze before dying in the blaze.

t: Ex-MP Muwanga Kivumbi Granted Bail in Inciting Violence Case
e: Former Butambala County MP and NUP Deputy President for Buganda, Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi, has been granted bail by the Butambala Chief Magistrate’s Court on charges of inciting violence and managing an unlawful society.

t: President Museveni Commissions Mbale Zoo, Urges Ugandans to Harness Tourism for Household Wealth
e: President Yoweri Museveni has commissioned the Mbale Wildlife Conservation Education Centre, urging residents in the Elgon Sub-region to tap into tourism to boost household incomes.

t: Kingfisher Oil Project Hits 99% Completion as Uganda Nears First Commercial Oil
e: The Kingfisher oil project's Central Processing Facility in Kikuube District is now 99 percent complete, with 22 of 31 planned production wells fully drilled and ready for operation.

t: UAE Eases Ebola-Related Travel Restrictions on Ugandan Nationals
e: The United Arab Emirates has lifted visa and entry restrictions on Ugandan citizens following the official conclusion of Uganda's Ebola outbreak.

t: Police Arrest Prime Suspect in Moses Matovu Murder, Reconstruct Crime Scene in Kibuli
e: Police have arrested private security guard Vincent Arnold Nsamba in connection with the fatal attack on Afrigo Band founder Moses Matovu following a crime scene reconstruction in Kibuli.

t: Afrigo Band Founder Moses Matovu Dies After Attack
e: Legendary musician and Afrigo Band founder Moses Matovu has died after being rushed to Kibuli Hospital following an attack in which he lost a lot of blood.

t: UNEB Releases 2026 Examination Timetables as Registration Reaches 1.63 Million Candidates
e: The Uganda National Examinations Board has released the official 2026 national examination timetables for PLE, UCE, and UACE, recording a 14.9 percent increase in candidate numbers.

t: Succession Dispute Forced Late King Oyo's Child to Remain in Texas, Says Queen Mother Kemigisa
e: Tooro Queen Mother Best Kemigisa has revealed that escalating leadership disputes following the death of King Oyo forced the royal family to leave his child in the United States.

t: Queen Mother Best Kemigisa Reveals Succession Dispute Forced King Oyo’s Child to Remain in Texas
e: Tooro Queen Mother Best Kemigisa has revealed that an intense succession dispute following the passing of Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV forced the royal family to keep the late King's child in Texas.

t: Uganda’s AirQo Named Finalist for 2026 Earthshot Prize
e: Makerere University-founded initiative AirQo has been selected as one of 15 global finalists for the prestigious 2026 Earthshot Prize for its low-cost air quality monitoring across African cities.

t: Bank of Uganda Warns Excessive Government Borrowing Risks Squeezing Private Sector Credit
e: Bank of Uganda Governor Michael Atingi-Ego has cautioned Parliament against exceeding the planned UGX 12.7 trillion domestic borrowing threshold, warning it could inflate interest rates and restrict credit to local businesses.

t: Sheikh Umar Convicted of Trafficking 13-Year-Old Niece, Sentenced to Time Served
e: The High Court has convicted Islamic cleric Sheikh Umar Muwonge Kamoga of aggravated child trafficking, sentencing him to the time he has already spent on remand.

t: General Court Martial Remands Maj Gen James Birungi After Surety Fails to Appear
e: The General Court Martial in Makindye has further remanded former Chief of Military Intelligence Maj Gen James Mugabe Birungi until September 24 after his surety failed to show up for his bail hearing.

t: Minister Bahati Rejects Wetland Site for Shs 20b Luwero Fruit Factory
e: State Minister for Trade David Bahati has rejected a 10-acre site acquired for the Shs 20 billion Luwero fruit processing factory after confirming the land is located in a protected wetland.

t: PLU Protests at Turkish Embassy Demanding Lumbuye Extradition as Critic Brands March a Political Show
e: Supporters of the Patriotic League of Uganda marched to the Turkish Embassy in Kampala demanding the return of Fred Lumbuye, while the Turkey-based critic dismissed the protest as a political publicity stunt.

t: Former UPDF Officer Michael Katungi Extradited to US Over Arms and Narcotics Charges
e: Former UPDF officer Michael Katungi Mpeirwe has been extradited from Luzira Prison to the United States to face trial on drug trafficking, firearms, and terrorism-related charges.

t: Museveni Launches Construction of Shs 1.2 Trillion Fuel Terminal in Mpigi
e: President Yoweri Museveni has commissioned the construction of the 320-million-litre Kampala Storage Terminal in Mpigi District to secure Uganda's fuel supply ahead of commercial oil production.

t: NRM’s James Leku Pilli Wins Adjumani West Parliamentary By-Election
e: National Resistance Movement candidate James Leku Pilli has been declared the new Member of Parliament for Adjumani West following a decisive victory in Thursday's by-election.

t: Government Sets Preliminary FY 2027/28 Budget Envelope at Shs 79.22 Trillion
e: The Ministry of Finance has reduced the preliminary resource envelope for the 2027/28 financial year to Shs 79.22 trillion as government seeks to cut borrowing and boost domestic revenue.

t: UWA and Partners Launch 10-Year Plan to Save Ishasha Lions
e: The Uganda Wildlife Authority and the Wildlife Conservation Society have launched a 10-year plan aimed at restoring the dwindling lion population in the Ishasha sector of Queen Elizabeth National Park, with an expected investment of about US$14 million.

t: Billions Invested in Uganda Railways but Assets Remain Unaccounted For
e: A new analysis has revealed that despite decades of heavy investment in Uganda’s railway system, there is no continuous and clear record of where many key assets, including wagons, ended up after the collapse of the East African Community and later concessions.

t: Standoff at King Oyo’s Burial Over Who Performs Key Ritual
e: A more than two-hour standoff erupted at Karambi Royal Tombs on Saturday as Queen Mother Best Kemigisa initially refused to allow the burial of her son to proceed over disagreement on who would perform the traditional nine coffee beans ritual, according to reports.

t: Calls Grow for New Hospital as Ageing Soroti Facility Struggles
e: Parliamentary Health Committee members and hospital managers have raised fresh concerns over the dilapidated state of Soroti Regional Referral Hospital, calling for construction of a new modern facility to serve the growing population.

t: King Oyo: The Boy King, the Succession War and a Kingdom Left in Uncertainty
e: From his death in the United States on 27 August 2026 to his burial at Karambi Royal Tombs exactly 31 years after his coronation, the story of Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV has been marked by grief, a bitter succession battle, high-level rituals, public tension and many unanswered questions that still hang over the Tooro Kingdom.

t: Museveni Orders Study of Plan to Turn City Square into Hotel and Mall
e: President Museveni has directed Minister Minsa Kabanda to evaluate a proposal by businessman Hajji Hassan Bulwadda to redevelop Kampala’s City Square into a solar-powered commercial complex with a hotel and shopping mall, sparking strong public opposition.

t: King Oyo Laid to Rest at Karambi Royal Tombs
e: Thousands of mourners gathered in Fort Portal on Saturday as the late Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV was buried at Karambi Royal Tombs after a solemn service at St John’s Cathedral, marking the end of his 31-year reign.

t: King Oyo Battled Rare Aggressive Cancer for Over a Year
e: Princess Ruth Komuntale has revealed that her brother, the late King Oyo, was diagnosed with angiosarcoma, a rare and aggressive cancer, in October 2025 after more than a year of unexplained pain and incorrect diagnoses.

t: King Oyo Buried on Exact Day He Was Crowned 31 Years Ago
e: In a powerful historical coincidence, Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV was laid to rest on 12 September 2026 — exactly 31 years after he was installed as King of Tooro as a three-year-old on the same date in 1995.

t: Museveni Appoints New Public Service Commission
e: President Yoweri Museveni has appointed nine new members to the Public Service Commission, naming Vincent Seruma as Chairperson and Jane Sanyu Mpagi as Deputy Chairperson.

t: President Confirms Nine Members Including Vincent Seruma as Chairperson and Jane Sanyu Mpagi as Deputy
e: President Yoweri Museveni has appointed nine new members to the Public Service Commission, naming Vincent Seruma as Chairperson and Jane Sanyu Mpagi as Deputy Chairperson.

t: Claims That UBC Anchor Declined Kingship Remain Unconfirmed as Succession Dispute Deepens Ahead of King Oyo’s Burial
e: Reports that Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma has rejected the Tooro throne are circulating, but no verified public statement from the UBC news anchor has emerged as the succession crisis intensifies one day before King Oyo’s burial.

t: Traders Cash In as Thousands of Mourners Flood Fort Portal for Final Send-Off
e: Business activity has surged around Karuziika Palace and across Fort Portal City as large numbers of mourners arrive for the burial of the late King Oyo.

t: Best Kemigisa Accuses Security of Restricting Movement at Karuziika Palace Amid Succession Row
e: Tooro Queen Mother Best Kemigisa has claimed that the royal family is under house arrest at Karuziika Palace after royal guards were removed and troops deployed, just days before the burial of King Oyo.

t: Four Official Speeches Allowed as Tooro Prepares Final Send-Off on 12 September
e: Tooro Kingdom has released the official burial programme for the late Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, restricting formal speeches to four speakers and setting a tightly timed schedule for the interment at Karambi Royal Tombs on 12 September.

t: Two Retired UPDF Generals Arrested in Intelligence Probe
e: Two retired UPDF generals who previously headed military intelligence, Maj Gen Abel Kandiho and Brig Gen Charles Bakahumura, have been arrested as investigations into alleged false intelligence and treachery continue.

t: Chris Obore and Six Others Granted Bail in Parliament Corruption Case
e: The Anti-Corruption Court has granted bail to interdicted Parliament Director of Communications Chris Obore and six co-accused facing charges linked to the alleged diversion of about Shs27 billion meant for parliamentary donations and CSR activities.

t: Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Named New King of Tooro
e: The Babiito royal clan has selected Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, a news anchor and editor with Uganda Broadcasting Corporation, as the new Omukama of Tooro following the death of King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV

t: Oyo’s Family Rejects Kijanangoma as New Tooro King
e: The family of the late Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV has rejected the announcement of Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma as the new King of Tooro, insisting the late monarch left a will identifying his son as the rightful heir.

t: AfDB Natural Resources Expert Named Successor to Ernest Rubondo as Uganda Edges Closer to First Oil
e: Fred Kabanda, currently heading the Non-Renewable Natural Resources Division at the African Development Bank, has been selected as the new Executive Director of the Petroleum Authority of Uganda, succeeding Ernest Rubondo whose second term ended on 31 August.

t: President Unveils Food Stabilisation Plan and Hails Recovery of 41,000 Guns as Peace Transforms Karamoja
e: President Yoweri Museveni on Wednesday attended the 11th Karamoja Cultural Festival in Moroto, where he praised the success of the government’s disarmament programme that recovered about 41,000 illegal guns and unveiled a three-phase strategy to end the region’s dependence on emergency food relief.

t: Deputy Speaker Tayebwa Endorses Gen Muhoozi for 2031 Presidency
e: Deputy Speaker of Parliament Thomas Tayebwa has publicly endorsed Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba as the preferred candidate to succeed President Yoweri Museveni in the 2031 general elections, describing the move as a civic expression of popular will.

t: Staffing Crisis Leaves Millions of Printed Cards Gathering Dust as Authority Seeks More Workers
e: The National Identification and Registration Authority is holding about 5.4 million newly printed national identity cards that citizens have not collected, a backlog attributed to severe understaffing after the mass enrolment exercise ended.

t: Bryan White Granted Bail After 293 Days on Remand
e: Kampala socialite Bryan Kirumira, popularly known as Bryan White, has been granted mandatory bail by the High Court after spending 293 days on remand over charges including human sacrifice and manslaughter linked to the death of a young woman.

t: Tooro Leaders Urge Government to Establish Regional Cancer Institute in Memory of Late Omukama Oyo
e: As Tooro Kingdom begins official mourning for Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, legislators from the region have called on the Government to establish a regional cancer institute in Fort Portal named after the late King, arguing that his death exposes the urgent need for accessible screening and treatment services beyond Kampala.

t: Body of King Oyo Arrives in Uganda
e: The body of the late Omukama of Tooro, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, arrived at Entebbe International Airport on 4 September 2026 and was received by President Yoweri Museveni before being transported to Karuziika Palace, marking the start of the official nine-day mourning period.

t: George Kamurasi Selected as Next King of Tooro
e: The Royal Succession Committee of Tooro Kingdom has selected 36-year-old George Desmond Kamurasi as the proposed successor to the late Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, with formal proclamation expected after the King’s burial on 12 September.

t: Global Ride-Hailing Giant Uber Shuts Down Operations in Uganda Effective 2 September
e: Uber has ended its ride-hailing operations in Uganda with immediate effect from 2 September 2026, closing a decade-long presence that began in Kampala in 2016, as part of a broader review that also saw it exit Nigeria.

t: Uganda and United States Seal Shs 6.4 Trillion Health Agreement with Shift to Government-to-Government Funding
e: Uganda and the United States have signed a Strategic Objective Agreement governing approximately $1.7 billion (Shs 6.42 trillion) in American health sector support from 2026 to 2030, marking a significant move toward direct government-to-government financing.

t: Schools to Reopen for Third Term on 14 September Full story headline: Ministry of Education Confirms Third Term
e: The Ministry of Education and Sports has reaffirmed that all pre-primary, primary and secondary schools under the national curriculum will reopen for Third Term on Monday, 14 September 2026, ending on 4 December, and has warned institutions against changing the official calendar without approval.

t: Mao Authorises Extradition of Michael Katungi to United States
e: Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Norbert Mao has authorised the extradition of Michael Katungi Mpeirwe to the United States, where he faces charges of conspiracy to traffic cocaine, possess firearms and provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organisation.

t: Witness Details Alleged Besigye Plot to Assassinate Museveni
e: The first prosecution witness in the treason trial of Dr Kizza Besigye has told the High Court that the opposition leader allegedly shared details of President Museveni’s movements and discussed assassinating him with drones or gunfire before creating a civil uprising to take power, claims the accused strongly deny.

t: Museveni Unveils ‘Pearl Sweet’ as Official Name for Uganda’s Crude Oil Ahead of First Exports
e: President Yoweri Museveni has officially named Uganda’s crude oil blend “Pearl Sweet” at a ceremony in Kikuube District, giving the resource a market identity that combines national pride with its low-sulphur quality as the country prepares for commercial production and exports later this year.

t: Tooro Forms 21-Member Committee to Identify King Oyo’s Successor
e: Tooro Kingdom has constituted a 21-member committee of Babiito clan elders to identify and formally announce the successor to the late Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV.

t: Boda Rider Shot Dead During National Cleaning Day Enforcement
e: A police officer has been arrested after shooting dead a boda boda rider in Ndejje during enforcement of movement restrictions on the second National Cleaning Day.

t: Minister Balaam Orders Arrests Over Alleged Market Fund Mismanagement and Revenue Leakages
e: Police have arrested the Town Clerk of Mbale City, the Industrial Division Town Clerk and the Mbale Central Market Master following directives by Local Government Minister Balaam Barugahara over alleged mismanagement of market funds.

t: Attorney General Warns Against Immediate Termination of Expressway Operator Contract
e: The Attorney General has cautioned against the immediate termination of the contract of the private operator of the Kampala–Entebbe Expressway, warning that failure to follow contractual procedures could expose Uganda to expensive international arbitration.

t: National Flags to Fly at Half-Mast for Three Days as President Reveals Late King Left a Young Son
e: President Yoweri Museveni has directed that the late Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV be accorded an official burial and that national flags fly at half-mast for three days. He also confirmed that the King left behind a young boy as heir.

t: Muhoozi Declares Intention to Contest 2031 Presidential Election
e: Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has publicly declared that he will contest the 2031 presidential election, saying he expects to win with the support of his father, President Yoweri Museveni.

t: Country Completes 42 Days Without New Confirmed Case After Containing Imported Outbreak
e: The World Health Organization and Africa CDC have declared Uganda free of Ebola after the country completed 42 consecutive days without a new confirmed case.

t: Iron Ore Leads Surge as Extractive Sector Records Strong Growth in FY 2023/24
e: Uganda’s mineral production value rose by 87 percent to Shs464.7 billion in the 2023/24 financial year, according to the latest Uganda Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative repor

t: WHO Hands Over Shs1.8 Billion Biosafety Level-3 Laboratory Funded by African Development Bank
e: The government has earmarked 120 traditional secondary schools for phased renovation, focusing on institutions constructed between the 1960s and 1980s that are losing learners to newer schools with better facilities.

t: BREAKING: Tooro Kingdom confirms the death of Omukama Oyo at 34. Buganda Kingdom expresses solidarity.
e: Tooro Kingdom has officially announced the death of Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV. The 34-year-old monarch passed away on Thursday evening. Buganda Kingdom has expressed solidarity with the people of Tooro.

t: E-Bus Express Launches New Electric Bus Routes in Kira
e: E-Bus Express has launched new electric bus routes in Kira Municipality, deploying locally manufactured Kayoola buses on three corridors as part of efforts to modernise public transport and ease congestion.

t: New Luxury Hotel and Executive Apartments in Nsambya Mark Debut of Marriott Brands in Uganda
e: President Yoweri Museveni on Thursday commissioned the Kampala Marriott Hotel and Marriott Executive Apartments in Nsambya, adding a new high-end hospitality facility to the capital’s skyline

t: Organisation Led by Gen Muhoozi Calls for Suspension of Funding and Dealings with Rwabwogo’s Committee
e: The Patriotic League of Uganda has asked the Ministry of Finance and other government agencies to halt an alleged Shs52 billion payment linked to the Presidential Advisory Committee on Exports and Industrial Development and suspend all dealings with the entity.

t: Former Speaker Will Not Face Prosecution as President Grants Mercy After Over 100 Days of Restriction
e: Former Speaker of Parliament Anita Among has been released from house arrest following a directive by President Yoweri Museveni. Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba announced that she will not be prosecuted.  Story body:

t: President Dismisses ‘Kutomera’ Concerns and Orders DPP to Fast-Track Prosecutions
e: President Yoweri Museveni has publicly defended the ongoing anti-corruption inspection tours by Local Government Minister Balaam Barugahara and State Minister Justine Nameere, calling for swift prosecution of those implicated.

t: Education Ministry Targets Ageing Infrastructure Built Between 1960s and 1980s in Phased Programme
e: The government has earmarked 120 traditional secondary schools for phased renovation, focusing on institutions constructed between the 1960s and 1980s that are losing learners to newer schools with better facilities.

t: Besigye Treason Trial: Witness Details Alleged Drone Plot and Fake Money Scheme
e: The treason trial of Dr Kizza Besigye continued this week with key testimony from American state witness Andrew Wilson, who alleged discussions of a drone assassination plot against President Museveni and plans to circulate counterfeit currency.

t: Alex Mukulu Laid to Rest with Official Funeral and Seven-Gun Salute
e: Veteran playwright, actor and cultural icon Alex Mukulu was laid to rest on Thursday with an official state funeral, including a seven-gun salute, in recognition of his decades-long contribution to Uganda’s creative industry.

t: Jambojet to Resume Nairobi–Entebbe Flights After Six-Year Break
e: Kenyan low-cost carrier Jambojet will resume daily flights between Nairobi and Entebbe on 1 October 2026, ending a six-year absence from the Ugandan market

t: Long-Serving Principal of Hillside Schools Naalya Passes Away After Collapsing During Medical Check-Up
e: Dr Henry Stanley Okia, the long-serving principal of Hillside Schools Naalya and a respected educationist with more than 40 years of service, has died. He collapsed while at a hospital for a medical check-up.

t: Kenyan Mother Allegedly Stabs Five Children in Kampala, Two Dead
e: A 43-year-old Kenyan woman is under investigation after allegedly stabbing her five children at their home in Kalungu-Bunga, Makindye Division, Kampala, killing two and injuring three others.

t: Local Government Minister Uncovers Inflated Costs and Shoddy Work at Panyimur Health Centre III During Anti-Corruption Tour
e: Minister of Local Government Balaam Barugahara was shocked during an inspection in Pakwach District after learning that a kitchen at Panyimur Health Centre III had cost Shs350 million amid other signs of poor workmanship and alleged mismanagement.

t: Five Kisoro District Officials Arrested Over Alleged Sale of Jobs
e: The State House Anti-Corruption Unit, working with CID, has arrested five Kisoro District Local Government officials, including the District Speaker and the Chairperson of the District Service Commission, over allegations of selling jobs.

t: Government Launches 100-Day Crackdown on Dangerous Taxis in Greater Kampala
e: The Ministry of Works and Transport has launched a 100-day enforcement operation to remove taxis in dangerous mechanical condition from roads in the Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area. Police will begin impounding the vehicles from Monday.

t: Cavendish University Graduates 1,059 Students at 15th Ceremony
e: Cavendish University Uganda has graduated 1,059 students from 33 nationalities at its 15th graduation ceremony. Chancellor and former Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan urged the Class of 2026 to focus on impact.

t: UEDCL Under Fire Over Persistent Outages and Rising Losses Since Umeme Takeover
e: Uganda Electricity Distribution Company Limited continues to face intense public and parliamentary criticism over frequent power outages, rising energy losses and slow connections since taking over from Umeme. Many customers say the situation has not improved and in some areas has worsened.

t: Balaam Calls for Tougher Anti-Corruption Measures in Local Governments
e: Minister of Local Government Balaam Barugahara has called for stronger anti-corruption and accountability measures in local governments, warning that the loss of public funds is directly denying citizens essential services.

t: Muhoozi Represents Uganda at Gabon’s 66th Independence Celebrations
e: Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba joined African heads of state in Gabon for the country’s 66th Independence Anniversary celebrations and held private talks with President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema.

t: Museveni Proposes Tax Exemption for Health Workers as Cabinet Restores Intern Pay
e: President Yoweri Museveni has proposed exempting health workers’ salaries from tax, while Cabinet has restored equal monthly facilitation for all medical interns in the current cohort after weeks of controversy.

t: IGG Interdicts URSB Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho and Three Senior Officials
e: The Inspector General of Government has ordered the interdiction of Uganda Registration Services Bureau Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho and three other senior officials. The move follows a presidential directive for an audit into alleged financial impropriety at the agency.

t: President Congratulates Officers for Contribution to Peace and Security, Advises Safe Investments
e: President Yoweri Museveni on Thursday presided over the retirement ceremony of 19 UPDF General Officers at State House, Entebbe. He congratulated them for their service and advised them on wise investment of their benefits.

t: Janet Museveni Joins President in Welcoming Bishop LaDonna Osborn at State House
e: President Yoweri Museveni and First Lady Janet Museveni on Wednesday hosted international evangelist Bishop Dr LaDonna C. Osborn at State House Entebbe ahead of the consecration of their daughter, Pastor Patience Rwabwogo.

t: Museveni Grants Official Burial to Veteran Playwright Alex Mukulu
e: President Yoweri Museveni has granted an official burial to celebrated Ugandan playwright, actor and director Alex Mukulu, who died on 15 August at the age of 72. The burial is scheduled for 20 August in Kijabijjo, Gayaza.

t: Besigye Treason Trial: Witness Reveals Spy Camera Hidden in Power Bank
e: A prosecution witness has told the High Court that a hidden camera inside a power bank was used to record meetings in which Dr Kizza Besigye allegedly discussed plans to acquire weapons and overthrow the government. The treason trial is proceeding with Besigye tried in absentia.

t: Uganda Approves and Advances UPDF Deployment to Gaza Stabilisation Force
e: Parliament has approved the deployment of a Uganda People’s Defence Forces contingent to the Gaza Strip as part of the proposed International Stabilisation Force. The move follows a request channelled through US President Donald Trump’s emissaries and is seen as carrying both security and diplomatic significance.

t: SC Villa Captain David Owori Beaten to Death by Robbers in Kampala
e: SC Villa captain and Uganda Cranes player David Owori has died after being brutally attacked by suspected robbers near his home in Makindye, Kampala. The 27-year-old was assaulted with paving stones after resisting the theft of his phone and belongings.

t: Deputy Speaker Commends Career of Integrity at Launch of Odongo’s Autobiography
e: Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa has described the career of UNEB Executive Director Dan Odongo as exemplary and one that should inspire public servants across Uganda. He spoke at the launch of Odongo’s book in Kampala.

t: Veteran Playwright and Actor Alex Mukulu Dies at 72
e: Veteran Ugandan playwright, actor, musician and theatre director Alex Mukulu has died at the age of 72. His death has left the country’s creative industry in mourning.

t: King Saha Packs Kololo to Capacity at Tondeka E’Kololo Festival
e: King Saha has filled Kololo Airstrip to maximum capacity for his Tondeka E’Kololo Festival. Crowds poured in throughout the day, turning the venue into a vibrant sea of music, fashion and celebration.

t: Court Delays Ruling as Prosecution Seeks to Block Live Coverage of Proceedings
e: The bail hearing of NUP Deputy President for Buganda, Hon Muwanga Kivumbi, has been adjourned to 25 August 2026. The prosecution is also seeking to stop live coverage of the court proceedings.

t: Six New Power Lines Completed as MPs Decry Limited Electricity Access
e: State Minister for Energy Sidronius Okaasai has announced the completion of six of eleven pending power lines, delivering 141,400 new electricity connections. At the same time, Members of Parliament have raised a general outcry over limited connectivity across the country.

t: Masaka SS Student Raped and Strangled as Wave of Attacks on Young Women Sparks Alarm
e: A Senior Four student at Masaka Secondary School, Rayati Nassali Nakato, has been found dead after being raped and strangled. The killing forms part of a disturbing pattern of recent attacks on young women that has left many Ugandans demanding stronger protection and faster police action.

t: CDF Urges Regional Forces to End Dependence on Unpredictable External Support and Fully Fund Standby Force
e: Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has urged Eastern African countries to build military independence and reduce reliance on external support. He made the call while opening the 36th Ordinary Session of the Eastern Africa Standby Force in Kampala

t: 12th Parliament Holds Inaugural Service Led by Archbishop Kaziimba
e: The Archbishop of the Church of Uganda, Dr Stephen Samuel Kaziimba Mugalu, has led the inaugural service for the 12th Parliament under the theme “Called to Serve.”

t: Armed Security Operatives Raid Musician’s Home with Reports of Gunfire Days Before Kololo Show
e: Musician King Saha was arrested on Tuesday evening after armed security personnel raided his apartment in Kyanja. The operation, which involved reports of gunfire, came as he promoted his concert scheduled for 14 August at Kololo Airstrip.

t: Seventh-day Adventists to Clean on Last Sunday of the Month Instead of Saturday
e: The Seventh-day Adventist Church has agreed with the Government of Uganda to conduct nationwide cleaning activities on the last Sunday of every month instead of Saturday, which is the official National Cleaning Day.

t: Museveni Swears In Three Ministers, Stresses Anti-Corruption and Loyalty
e: President Yoweri Museveni on Tuesday swore in three ministers at State House Entebbe: Ambassador Adonia Ayebare as Foreign Affairs Minister, Shartsi Kutesa Musherure as State Minister for Micro-Finance, and Juma Witonze as State Minister for Internal Affairs.

t: President Directs Mariam Wangadya to Continue Serving as Human Rights Commission Boss
e: President Yoweri Museveni has rejected the resignation of Uganda Human Rights Commission Chairperson Mariam Fauzat Wangadya and instructed her to remain in office. Wangadya revealed this while appearing before Parliament’s COSASE committee.

t: Committee Pauses Review of Auditor General’s Report as Two Officials Claim CEO Position at Insurance Regulatory Authority
e: Parliament’s Committee on Commissions, Statutory Authorities and State Enterprises has paused scrutiny of the Auditor General’s report on the Insurance Regulatory Authority after two individuals appeared claiming the position of Chief Executive Officer.

t: First Daughter Thanks God as First Lady Reappears After Months Away from Public Eye
e: Natasha Museveni Karugire has shared fresh photos with her mother, First Lady Janet Museveni, after months of limited public appearances due to illness. She captioned the post “Thank you, LORD Jesus!”

t: Susan Magara Sentencing Sparks Debate on Islamic Dress in Court and Collective Blame
e: The High Court has sentenced nine people in the 2018 kidnap and murder of Susan Magara, with two receiving the death penalty. Public debate has shifted to the convicts’ Islamic attire in court and the risks of collective blame against the Muslim community.

t: CEO Musanya Musa Reflects on Journey from COVID-19 Idea to Technology, Media and Education Brands
e: KMVTECHUG is marking its sixth anniversary. What began as a YouTube channel during the COVID-19 pandemic has grown into an ecosystem of media, technology and education brands under the leadership of CEO Musanya Musa.

t: Ruhamya Kainerugaba Graduates from Sandhurst as Father Looks On
e: Officer Cadet Ruhamya Kainerugaba, son of Chief of Defence Forces Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba and grandson of President Museveni, has graduated from the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst. Fellow Ugandan Andrew Bakira Ruyondo was awarded the International Sword.

t: Youth Parliament Adopts Key Motions on Sexual and Reproductive Health, Climate Action and Road Safety
e: Following the reproductive health motion, the House adopted a resolution on climate action, environmental protection and the building of climate-resilient communities. Youth delegates highlighted the disproportionate impact of climate change on young people and called for stronger government interventions in environmental protection and community resilience.

t: Health Minister Baryomunsi Visits Besigye at Mulago, Says He Is Steadily Recovering
e: Health Minister Dr Chris Baryomunsi has visited Dr Kizza Besigye at Mulago National Referral Hospital and reported that the veteran opposition leader is steadily recovering. Besigye has been in detention for nearly two years.

t: Two Next Media Journalists Killed in Entebbe Road Crash, Colleague in ICU
e: Two employees of Next Media Services, Badru Kasirye and Isaac Ndamagye, have died in a road accident along Entebbe Road early Friday morning. Their colleague Brian “Makona” Ssemanda is in intensive care

t: Ogwang Assures Parliament that Aki-Bua Stadium and Other Venues Will Meet CAF Standards
e: Sports Minister Peter Ogwang has told Parliament that government is on course to deliver three stadiums to host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. CAF has agreed that Aki-Bua Stadium can host matches if required standards are met.

t: Museveni in Tanzania at Invitation of President Samia Suluhu Hassan to Strengthen Bilateral Ties
e: President Yoweri Museveni has arrived in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, for a two-day official visit at the invitation of President Samia Suluhu Hassan. The visit aims to strengthen Uganda-Tanzania relations.

t: Kiryowa Kiwanuka Seeks Parliamentary Support for UPDF Priorities and Ongoing Programmes
e: Defence Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka appeared before the Parliamentary Committee on Defence and Internal Affairs to present the state of the Ministry of Defence and Veterans Affairs, key achievements and resource requirements for the UPDF.

t: Two Sentenced to Death, Seven Get Life in Susan Magara Murder Case
e: The High Court has sentenced Hajara Nakandi and Abbas Musa Buwembo to death for their central roles in the 2018 kidnap and murder of Susan Magara. The remaining seven convicts received life imprisonment.

t: Musasizi and Lugoloobi Urge Enterprise Uganda to Leverage Technology for Wider Entrepreneurship Support
e: Finance Minister Henry Musasizi and State Minister for Planning Amos Lugoloobi have challenged Enterprise Uganda to use digital platforms to reach more Ugandans with entrepreneurship and business support services.

t: Malende Raises Kampala Garbage Crisis in Parliament as Government Pledges Action
e: Kampala Woman MP Shamim Malende has raised the continued accumulation of uncollected garbage in parts of the city as a matter of national importance. Government responded that KCCA is scaling up efforts and will provide additional trucks.

t: Besigye Unable to Appear in Court as Prisons Officer Confirms He Remains at Mulago
e: A prisons officer has informed the High Court that Dr Kizza Besigye remains admitted at Mulago Hospital and cannot appear for his treason trial. The defence has asked that a medical doctor present the health report instead.

t: Pepsi Uganda Welcomes Ghetto Kids Home After World Cup Final Performance
e: Pepsi Uganda has officially welcomed home the Ghetto Kids following their historic performance at the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final halftime show. The young dancers shared the stage with global stars Shakira and Burna Boy.

t: URSB Deregisters 90,000 Inactive Companies in Massive Compliance Crackdown
e: The Uganda Registration Services Bureau has officially deregistered 90,000 companies that failed to file annual returns for five consecutive years and did not apply for restoration within the given grace period. The action was taken under the Companies Act.

t: UPDF Pulls Out of NMG Offices After Weeks of Occupation as Management Conducts Safety Checks
e: The Uganda People’s Defence Forces have finally withdrawn from the premises of Nation Media Group Uganda. Management has, however, advised staff not to return immediately as the company’s internal security team continues safety and security assessments.

t: 14 Killed in Fatal Crash Between Taxi and Sand Truck in Lwera Swamp
e: Fourteen people died on the spot in a fatal road accident in Lwera Swamp, Kalungu District, on the night of 3 August 2026. A Toyota Hiace taxi collided with a Sino truck carrying sand along the Kampala–Masaka Highway.

t: Works Minister Directs Contractor to Speed Up Kira–Kasangati–Matugga Road
e: Works and Transport Minister Fred Byamukama has directed the contractor on the Kira–Kasangati–Matugga Road to immediately accelerate works following the resolution of key land issues. Clear deadlines have been set for critical sections of the project.

t: Nambeshe Welcomes Nine NUP Supporters Freed After More Than Six Years in Detention
e: NUP Acting President and Manjiya MP John Baptist Nambeshe on Monday officially welcomed nine party supporters who regained their freedom after more than six years in detention. The group was released last week through the Amnesty Commission process.

t: High Court Convicts All Nine Accused in Susan Magara Kidnap and Murder Case
e: The High Court in Kampala has convicted all nine accused persons in the 2018 kidnap and murder of businesswoman Susan Magara. Justice Alex Mackay Ajiji ruled that the prosecution proved the charges of kidnap with intent to procure a ransom and murder beyond reasonable doubt. Sentencing is scheduled for Tuesday.

t: Museveni Presents Olara Otunnu as Uganda’s Candidate for UN Secretary-General
e: President Yoweri Museveni on Monday formally presented Ambassador Olara Otunnu as Uganda’s candidate for the position of United Nations Secretary-General. He urged ambassadors of UN Security Council member states to convey Uganda’s endorsement to their governments.

t: President Museveni Hits Back at Andrew Mwenda Over Stephen Nuwagaba, Insists Torture Has No Place in the Struggle
e: President Yoweri Museveni has strongly rejected journalist Andrew Mwenda’s claims that Stephen Nuwagaba has laid “siege” on State House and security agencies. In a detailed statement, the President describes Nuwagaba as a torture victim he rescued and reaffirms that torture remains immoral and counter-revolutionary.

t: Bayigga and Spire Challenge President Museveni Over Condition of Missing Activist Sam Mugumya
e: Buikwe South MP Dr Bayigga Lulume and philosopher-cartoonist Jim Spire Ssentongo have publicly challenged President Yoweri Museveni over the leaked video of long-missing opposition activist Sam Mugumya. Both posts question the continued silence and suffering amid official denials of his detention.

t: Dr Moses Mukose Freed on Bond After Overnight Detention for Being Near Kizza Besigye’s Hospital Room
e: Dr Moses Mukose has been released on police bond after spending more than 20 hours in custody. He was arrested at Mulago National Referral Hospital for allegedly wandering on the VIP floor where Dr Kizza Besigye is admitted under tight security.

t: Bamasaba Kick Off 2026 Imbalu Cultural Festival at Mutoto as Nambeshe Calls for Unity and Development
e: The 2026 Imbalu Cultural Festival was officially launched at Mutoto Cultural Grounds in Mbale City. NUP Acting President and Manjiya MP John Baptist Nambeshe attended and urged the Bamasaba community to unite for development while celebrating their biennial rite of passage to manhood.

t: Leaked Video Showing Frail Sam Mugumya Reignites Outrage Over Enforced Disappearances
e: A video shared by NUP leader Robert Kyagulanyi (Bobi Wine) purporting to show long-missing opposition activist Sam Mugumya has triggered fresh national and international concern. The footage depicts a frail Mugumya using a walking frame. Security agencies have previously denied holding him.

t: IGG Directs Immediate Interdiction of Chris Obore and Six Senior Parliament Officials Over Corruption
e: Inspector General of Government Lady Justice Naluzze Aisha Batala has directed the Clerk to Parliament to immediately interdict Chris Obore and six other senior officials currently facing corruption charges. The order takes effect while their cases remain before the Anti-Corruption Court.

t: Kyambogo University Under Fire Over Wrong Certificates Awarded to Graduates
e: Kyambogo University has come under scrutiny after Members of Parliament discovered that some graduates were awarded certificates for courses they never studied. The revelation emerged during a session of the Parliamentary Committee on Education and Sports. Lawmakers heard that students admitted for programmes leading to Diplomas in Physical Education and Sports instead received certificates in Sports Management

t: Kabaka Mutebi II Marks 33 Years on the Throne as Buganda Celebrates Amatikkira33 in Style at Watoto Church
e: Buganda Kingdom on Friday staged a colourful and historic thanksgiving service to mark the 33rd coronation anniversary of His Majesty Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II, drawing thousands of subjects, cultural leaders, government officials, opposition figures, and religious leaders to Watoto Church in Bweyogerere.

t: LoP Joel Ssenyonyi Joins Buganda Kingdom Thanksgiving for Kabaka Mutebi II’s 33rd Coronation Anniversary
e: Bweyogerere, Uganda — Leader of Opposition Joel Ssenyonyi on Friday attended a special thanksgiving service at Watoto Church in Bweyogerere to mark the 33rd anniversary of the coronation of Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II of Buganda. Ssenyonyi joined other political, cultural, and religious leaders in honouring the Kabaka’s three decades on the throne, a milestone symbolising unity, cultural resilience, and development within the kingdom.

t: PM Nabbanja Joins Buganda Kingdom for Historic #Amatikkira33 Celebrations at Watoto Church
e: Bweyogerere, Uganda — Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja on Friday led government representation at Watoto Church in Bweyogerere as the Buganda Kingdom marked the 33rd anniversary of the coronation of Kabaka Ronald Muwenda Mutebi II.

t: She Cranes Blaze Past Scotland! Uganda Delivers Dominant 65-56 Thrashing at Commonwealth Games
e: Glasgow, Scotland — Uganda’s She Cranes delivered a commanding performance in netball as they defeated hosts Scotland 65-56 in a Pool B encounter at the Commonwealth Games. The win showcased the growing strength and tactical maturity of Ugandan women’s netball on the global stage.

t: President Museveni Hosts UK MP to Strengthen Uganda-UK Healthcare Partnership
e: President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni on Thursday welcomed Hon. Beccy Cooper MP, Chair of the UK All-Party Parliamentary Group on Global Health, for discussions focused on deepening bilateral ties in the health sector.

t: Lira District Officials Jailed Four Years Each for Land Fraud and Abuse of Office
e: “The three public officials were each sentenced to four years’ imprisonment and will not hold any public office for the next 10 years, while Atoo Rebecca was sentenced to one year in prison.” — Anti-Corruption Unit statement.

t: Anti-Corruption Court Remands OPM Commissioner and IT Officer Over Alleged Abuse of Office
e: “The prosecution of the two officials underscores the IGG’s unwavering resolve to combat corruption and abuse of public office.” — Inspectorate of Government statement.

t: Parliament Vets Juma Witonze Kisekka as New Minister of State for Internal Affairs
e: Uganda’s Parliament Appointments Committee has successfully vetted Hon. Juma Witonze Kisekka, President Yoweri Museveni’s nominee for Minister of State for Internal Affairs. The process, completed on Thursday morning, paves the way for his formal appointment following a swift review of his credentials.

t: Idi Amin’s Grandson Disqualified in Commonwealth Games Boxing Quarter-Final
e: “I might be the new King of Scotland. It’s possible... I have that dream that I’m gonna go back with gold medal. That’s the reason I’m here in Glasgow right now.” — Aziz Abdul (Ringo), ahead of the quarter-final.

t: Busoga University Reopening Delayed as Government Awaits Museveni’s Verdict on Name
e: “Some people wanted it to remain Busoga University, while others proposed Kiira University and other names. We have now concluded the consultations and are left with only one stakeholder, the President.” — Dr John Chrysostom Muyingo, Acting Minister of Education and Sports.

t: FORMER MP MUWANGA KIVUMBI ARRAIGNED IN COURT AFTER ABDUCTION CLAIMS
e: Former Butambala County Member of Parliament Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi has been charged with incitement to violence and remanded to prison after appearing before the Butambala Magistrates Court on Wednesday. The development follows his dramatic reappearance after over two weeks of being missing.

t: JUDICIARY TIGHTENS MEDIA ACCESS RULES FOR BESIGYE TREASON CASE
e: The Judiciary of Uganda has issued revised guidelines for the high profile treason trial of retired Colonel Kizza Besigye and two others. The new rules focus on security screening and access controls as the case resumes amid heightened public interest.

t: DR KIZZA BESIGYE COLLAPSES IN COURT AS TREASON TRIAL DRAGS ON
e: Retired Colonel Kizza Besigye was rushed to hospital on Wednesday after he fainted in the High Court during his ongoing treason trial. Court proceedings were immediately suspended. The incident has once again thrown the spotlight on the prolonged legal battle and the political tensions surrounding the opposition veteran.

t: BUGANDA RELEASES NEW ARRANGEMENT OF NATIONAL ANTHEM
e: The Katikkiro of Buganda  Charles Peter Mayiga  has officially released a refreshed version of the kingdom's national anthem  Ekitiibwa kya Buganda. The announcement came through a post on X today  featuring a performance by the St. Charles Lwanga Lubaga Cathedral Choir.

t: Nation Media Group Uganda Cleared to Resume Operations After June Shutdown
e: In a significant development for media freedom in Uganda, Nation Media Group (NMG) Uganda, publishers of Daily Monitor and operators of NTV Uganda and other platforms  has been cleared to resume full operations following a government-mandated shutdown in June 2026.

t: President Museveni Appoints Hon. Juma Witonze Kisekka as Minister of State for Internal Affairs
e: In a latest cabinet adjustment, President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has appointed Hon. Juma Witonze Kisekka (also referred to as Juma Witonze) as the new Minister of State for Internal Affairs. The appointment, announced on July 27, 2026, is pending parliamentary approval, in line with constitutional requirements.

t: Police Urge Peace and Order as Uganda Prepares for Local Council Elections Today
e: With campaigns closed yesterday (Monday, July 27, 2026) and voting scheduled for today Tuesday, July 28, 2026, the Uganda Police Force has issued a strong public reminder to candidates, their supporters, and the general public to uphold peace, lawfulness, and order throughout the Local Council (LC) elections.

t: Police Intensify Crackdown on Illegal Charcoal Trade in West Nile: Eight Suspects Arrested as Environmental Protection Efforts Gain Momentum
e: In a decisive joint operation, Uganda Police Forces Environmental Protection Police Unit (EPPU), working alongside the Uganda Peoples Defence Forces (UPDF) and the National Forestry Authority (NFA), has arrested eight suspects in Madi Okollo District and surrounding areas of the West Nile sub-region for illegal dealing in charcoal. The operation, conducted on July 25, 2026, resulted in the impoundment of 72 bags of charcoal, now secured as exhibits at Madi Okollo Police Station.

t: Uganda Nominates Dr. Olara Otunnu for UN Secretary-General: A Bold Diplomatic Masterstroke or Calculated Distraction?
e: In a surprise move that has sparked both excitement and skepticism, Uganda has officially nominated veteran diplomat and former presidential candidate Dr. Olara Otunnu for the position of United Nations Secretary-General. The announcement has ignited fresh debate about Ugandaâs foreign policy ambitions and the timing of this high-profile nomination.

t: DPP vs Doctors: Is Ugandas Justice System Sacrificing Erias Lukwagos Health on the Altar of Politics?
e: A troubling rift has emerged in the high-profile case of former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago. t: National Cleaning Day: A Bold National Initiative Marred by Coercion and Controversy
e: Uganda's inaugural National Cleaning Day drew praise for civic mobilisation but sharp criticism after videos showed police using roadblocks and force to enforce participation.

t: Muwanga Kivumbi: Two Weeks of Silence After Televised Abduction Where Is the Rule of Law?
e: Sixteen days after his interception at a Mpigi roadblock, Muwanga Kivumbi's whereabouts remain officially unknown, as police deny holding him and a habeas corpus process unfolds.

t: Muhoozi in Kigali: Military Diplomacy or Succession Signal Amid Domestic Shadows?
e: Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba's two-day working visit to Kigali showcases regional military diplomacy, even as domestic concerns over abductions and succession politics intensify.

t: Erias Lukwago's Bail Bid: Health Crisis or High-Stakes Political Chess?
e: The High Court is set to rule on Erias Lukwago's bail application on July 30, as his legal team cites a litany of serious health conditions worsened by prolonged detention.

t: Karamoja Hunger Crisis: Emergency Relief Meets Accusations of Neglect and Exploitation
e: As government and WFP roll out emergency food relief in Karamoja, critics accuse a high-profile land initiative of diverting harvests away from the very communities it promised to feed.

t: Gen. Moses Ali Laid to Rest in Adjumani: A Nation Bids Farewell to a Veteran Statesman
e: Gen. Moses Ali has been laid to rest at his ancestral home in Adjumani, closing days of national mourning that included a lying-in-state at Parliament and tributes from President Museveni.

t: Court Gives Security Agencies 3 Days to Account for Missing Muwanga Kivumbi Amid Mounting Pressure and Rumours
e: High Court Justice Collins Acellam orders the CDF and IGP to report within three days on Muwanga Kivumbi's whereabouts, as unconfirmed rumours of torture continue to swirl.

t: Body of Gen. Moses Ali Flown to Adjumani as Parliament Pays Glowing Tributes
e: President Museveni and Parliament pay emotional tribute to Gen. Moses Ali as his body is airlifted to Adjumani, ahead of burial tomorrow, Wednesday July 23.

t: High Court to Hear Erias Lukwago Bail Application on July 24 Amid Health Concerns and Treason-Related Charges
e: The High Court will hear Erias Lukwago's bail application on July 24, as a Mulago medical report details serious chronic conditions worsened during his remand.

t: Uganda Accelerates Cashless Drive: Cash Tolls Set for Phase-Out on Kampala-Entebbe Expressway
e: Government moves to phase out cash payments at Kampala-Entebbe Expressway toll plazas in favour of mobile money and electronic tag systems, part of a wider digital payments push.

t: KCCA Admits Procedural Lapses in Tycoon Ham's Nakivubo Channel Project as Parliament Scrutinizes Urban Development

t: Mixed Emotions as Eddy Kenzo Earns Grammy Nomination but Misses the Ceremony
e: Eddy Kenzo secures a Best African Music Performance nomination at the 2026 Grammys, but personal circumstances prevent him from attending the Los Angeles ceremony.
